doc.title: Jack DeJohnette — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: New York and the Lloyd quartet
title: Birdland visit and hearing Miles Davis's quintet
summary: He sits in on drums and piano at Birdland, sees Tony Williams, and recalls hearing Miles's quintet.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: You'll get it, and Earl Grey. Did Earl Grey play trombone? Because they were kind of a team. Al somebody… …anyway, so I played piano. I sat in on piano, played “Well You Needn't.”
Yeah, Birdland. I first played… sat in on drums, and then I sat in on piano. And I remember Tony Williams was in the house then.
And he was already with Miles at this time.

He was with Miles then. I heard that Miles Davis Quintet when George Coleman was in the group. They came through Chicago when Seven Steps To Heaven came out. I remember, because they all had jackets with their names on them. Miles had these gray jackets they all had to wear with their names on them.
Really? Miles had his guys wear uniforms?
